artists.biography: Tim Bowness is a british singer/songwriter primarily known for his work as part of the band No-Man, a long-term project with Steven Wilson from Porcupine Tree.  In addition to producing several albums with No-Man, Tim has recorded with popular Italian artist Alice, experimental guitar legend David Torn, Soft Machine's Hugh Hopper, Roger Eno, German band Centrozoon, and recorded the album Flame (1994) in collaboration with Porcupine Tree/ex-Japan keyboard player Richard Barbieri.  Tim's debut solo album, My Hotel Year, was released on the One Little Indian label in 2004.

Tim Bowness.biography: Tim Bowness is a british singer/songwriter primarily known for his work as part of the band No-Man, a long-term project with Steven Wilson from Porcupine Tree.  In addition to producing several albums with No-Man, Tim has recorded with popular Italian artist Alice, experimental guitar legend David Torn, Soft Machine's Hugh Hopper, Roger Eno, German band Centrozoon, and recorded the album Flame (1994) in collaboration with Porcupine Tree/ex-Japan keyboard player Richard Barbieri.  Tim's debut solo album, My Hotel Year, was released on the One Little Indian label in 2004.

perplexity.description:
Late Night Laments," released on August 28, 2020, is the sixth solo album by English singer-songwriter Tim Bowness, issued through Inside Out Music and Sony Music. The album blends elements of electronic, rock, and pop within a predominantly melancholic and moody atmosphere, characterized by Bowness' whispered vocals and introspective lyrics. It marks a continuation of his exploration into progressive and art pop styles but with a notably darker and more intimate tone, as exemplified by tracks like "I'm Better Now," which features unconventional harmonies and a Fripp-inspired guitar solo that enhances its menacing mood.

Musically, "Late Night Laments" stands out for its subtle yet sophisticated production, combining synths, guitars, and programmed drums to create a soundscape suited for late-night listening. The album was crafted in two main creative periods between 2019 and early 2020, with contributions from longtime collaborator Brian Hulse and mixing by Steven Wilson, ensuring a polished and atmospheric finish. Critically, it has been regarded as a significant step forward in Bowness' solo discography, praised for its songwriting depth and emotional resonance, making it one of his most consistent and compelling works to date.
